sections.label: ASEAN in school curricula
sections.summary: Social Studies, History, Geography and Economics teach students about ASEAN at primary, secondary and pre-university levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: In primary Social Studies, students are introduced to the origins, member countries and purposes of ASEAN as part of appreciating how communities in ASEAN member countries are connected through cultural, economic and geographical ties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: At the secondary level, students expand their understanding of ASEAN and its member countries through subjects like History, Geography and Social Studies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Students study the key forces and events that shaped the histories of Southeast Asian member countries and appreciate the importance of ASEAN in forging friendly relations with countries in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: They explore environmental issues related to the social and economic development in Southeast Asia and learn about the role of ASEAN in maintaining regional stability and security.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: At the pre-university level, students deepen their understanding of the opportunities and challenges confronting ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Through History, students discuss the effectiveness of ASEAN in promoting peace, security and economic development in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: They examine the role of the ASEAN Free Trade Area in regional economic development in Economics and Geography.

sections.label: International Friendship Day commemoration
sections.summary: The annual International Friendship Day celebrates regional diversity and stresses good relations between Singapore and its neighbours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: For instance, the annual commemoration of International Friendship Day celebrates the region's diversity and emphasises the importance of good relations between Singapore and her neighbours.

sections.label: ASEAN Schools Games
sections.summary: Through the ASEAN Schools Games, student athletes compete, build friendships and gain cultural awareness of fellow ASEAN athletes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: In addition, through the ASEAN Schools Games, our student athletes not only spar with the region’s best, they also forge friendships and gain greater cultural awareness of their fellow athletes from the different ASEAN countries.
